crash.title: Crash helper

out-of-memory.title: Not enough memory
out-of-memory.text: The server had {{memoryMb}} MB and needed more. This often happens with modpacks or many players.
out-of-memory.fix: Give the server more memory (e.g. 2 GB more) and restart it.

wrong-java.title: Wrong Java version
wrong-java.text: Part of the server needs Java {{java}}, but a different version was started.
wrong-java.fix: Set the Java version to “Automatic” or Java {{java}} in the settings.

missing-dependency.title: A required plugin or mod is missing
missing-dependency.text: {{plugin}} needs {{dependency}}, which is not installed. {{plugin}} itself is fine.
missing-dependency.fix: Install {{dependency}} – with the button below (matching your version) or from the marketplace.

port-in-use.title: The port is already in use
port-in-use.text: Another program or server already uses this port.
port-in-use.fix: Pick a free port in the settings (e.g. 25566) and restart.

eula.title: Minecraft EULA not accepted
eula.text: The server does not start without agreeing to the EULA.
eula.fix: Start the server again; MorniHosting sets the agreement automatically.

version-not-found.title: This version does not exist
version-not-found.text: The selected game version could not be downloaded.
version-not-found.fix: Pick a different version in the settings.

mod-version-mismatch.title: Mods do not match the game version
mod-version-mismatch.text: At least one mod was built for a different Minecraft version.
mod-version-mismatch.fix: Check the mods for updates in the marketplace or remove the mismatching mod.

world-broken.title: The world cannot be loaded
world-broken.text: The world files seem to be damaged.
world-broken.fix: Restore a backup. Under “Backups” that takes one click.

plugin-error.title: A plugin is causing trouble
plugin-error.fix: Update {{plugin}} or switch it off under “Plugins” for now.

start-failed.title: The server could not start
start-failed.fix: Check that Docker is running and try again.

unknown.title: Unknown cause
unknown.text: The server stopped unexpectedly (code {{exitCode}}). The last lines below usually give a hint.
unknown.fix: Restart the server. If it happens again, take a close look at the console.

download-failed.title: Game files could not be downloaded
download-failed.text: On its first start the server downloads the game files from the internet. That failed.
download-failed.fix: Check the server's internet connection (DNS, firewall) and start it again.

crash.fixedStarting: Fixed – the server is starting again.

danger.restore-backup: The world and all files go back to the backup. The panel makes a safety backup first.
danger.reset-world: The broken world is deleted (it goes to the bin, with a backup made first). On the next start the server creates a new world.

disk-full.title: The disk is full
disk-full.text: The server could not save anything: there is no free space left on the machine.
disk-full.fix: Delete old backups or files (empty the trash) or give the machine more disk space.

host-out-of-memory.title: The machine ran out of memory
host-out-of-memory.text: The server ({{memoryMb}} MB) was killed because the whole machine had no memory left – usually too many servers or one with more RAM than the machine.
host-out-of-memory.fix: Give the server less RAM, stop other servers or give the machine more RAM (Proxmox: pct set <ID> --memory …).

plugin-incompatible.title: {{plugin}} does not fit this server version
plugin-incompatible.text: {{plugin}} was built for another Minecraft version and calls things that do not exist here.
plugin-incompatible.fix: Update {{plugin}} under “Plugins” or switch it off until there is an update.

world-locked.title: The world is already open
world-locked.text: Something else still holds the world open (an old server process or a second server with the same world).
world-locked.fix: Wait a moment and restart. If it happens again, delete session.lock in the world folder.

config-broken.title: A settings file has an error
config-broken.text: A config file (YAML/JSON) is broken, often a tab, a missing space or quote.
config-broken.fix: Open the last changed file under “Files” and fix the line from the error below.

config-broken-plugin.title: The settings of {{plugin}} are broken
config-broken-plugin.text: A config file of {{plugin}} has a typo (often a tab or missing quotes).
config-broken-plugin.fix: Open the folder plugins/{{plugin}} under “Files” and fix the file, or switch {{plugin}} off for now.

watchdog.title: The server froze
watchdog.text: One game tick took so long that the watchdog stopped the server (too much going on, an endless loop or too little CPU).
watchdog.fix: Restart. If it happens often, reduce farms/entities or give the server more CPU.

watchdog-plugin.title: {{plugin}} froze the server
watchdog-plugin.text: The watchdog stopped the server because {{plugin}} took too long.
watchdog-plugin.fix: Update {{plugin}} or switch it off and restart.

permission-denied.title: No permission for files
permission-denied.text: The server was not allowed to read or write a file.
permission-denied.fix: Restart the server; MorniHosting fixes the permissions. Only upload files through the panel.

unknown-error.title: The server crashed with an error
unknown-error.fix: Restart. If the error comes back, search for the message or switch off recently installed plugins/mods.

ddos.honestTitle: What the protection can do – and what not
ddos.honestText: It helps against single troublemakers and small floods: bots connecting thousands of times, or someone flooding your Bedrock port. Against big attacks that clog your whole internet line nothing running at your home helps – the line is full before a packet reaches your computer. Only a service in front of your connection helps there:

If you created the container yourself, NetBird needs a network device there: add these two lines on the Proxmox host to /etc/pve/lxc/<ID>.conf and restart the container:
netbird.step1Router: Does NetBird already run on another device in your home network (as a router)? Then a resource for {{ip}} under Networks is enough – you pick it as the target later.
netbird.step2Add: In the NetBird dashboard: Reverse Proxy → Custom Domains → Add Domain. Enter this domain (without *) and save:
netbird.step2Dns: Then add this record at your domain provider (NetBird shows the exact value after saving):
netbird.step2Verify: Back at NetBird: Verify Domain → Start Verification. Once it says Active, continue. Usually this takes a few minutes, at most 24 hours.
netbird.step3Title: Make the panel reachable over HTTPS
netbird.step3Add: Reverse Proxy → Services → Add Service, then Add Target. As target, pick Peer and your MorniHosting machine – or Host with the IP below if NetBird runs on another device in your home network:
netbird.step3Host: Under Settings, best turn on Pass Host Header. Then the panel sees your domain directly (signing in and passkeys also work without it).

selfHosted.title: Self-hosted NetBird: open the ports
selfHosted.fixed: The NetBird proxy only lets port 443 through by default. Open these ports once – in your NetBird server's docker-compose.yml under the netbird-proxy service, then run “docker compose up -d”. New servers get the next free port (25566, 25567 …); easiest is to open a range right away, e.g. “25565-25575:25565-25575/tcp”.
selfHosted.random: The NetBird proxy only lets port 443 through by default, and your NetBird assigns its own port per server. Open each of these ports – in your NetBird server's docker-compose.yml under the netbird-proxy service, then run “docker compose up -d”. If your proxy allows custom ports, MorniHosting uses the servers' own ports (25565 …) automatically.
selfHosted.firewall: If your provider has its own firewall in the customer panel (e.g. IONOS, Hetzner), open the same ports there – no script can reach it. By hand works too: add the ports above to netbird-proxy in docker-compose.yml, or run the proxy with “network_mode: host”.
selfHosted.auto: Easiest: run this command once on your NetBird server. It opens 25565–25575/tcp, 19132–19140/udp and 24454–24460/udp on netbird-proxy (and in ufw/firewalld if active) and restarts only the proxy.

mail.title: Sending e-mail
mail.text: With a mailbox (SMTP) the panel can send mails. Without these settings everything works as before.
mail.hostHint: The address of the outgoing server, e.g. smtp.example.com.
mail.securityHint: “TLS” (port 465) and “STARTTLS” (port 587) are both secure. Not sure? The test below tries both. “None” only inside your own network.
mail.passwordHint: Stored encrypted and never shown again.
mail.passwordKept: A password is saved. Leave empty to keep it.
mail.fromHint: How the mail appears to the recipient, e.g. MorniHosting <noreply@mornihosting.de>.
mail.needsDomain: Links in mails need the panel's domain (tab “Domain & HTTPS”). Until then sign-up and “password forgotten” stay off.
mail.registration: Allow sign-up on the start page
mail.registrationHint: New people create their own account and must confirm their e-mail address with a link. They only get standard rights.
mail.registrationOrdersHint: Only applies when new accounts start without approval. Anyone you accept under Approvals may always order servers.
mail.crashMails: Mail admins when a server crashes
mail.crashMailsHint: At most one mail per server every 15 minutes, in addition to webhooks.
mail.testHint: Leave empty to send it to your own address (My account).
mail.helpTitle: Where do I get a mail server?
mail.helpInwx: INWX: create a mailbox for noreply@your-domain in the customer menu. Server and port are in the mailbox details (usually mail.inwx.de, port 587).
mail.helpIonos: IONOS: create a mailbox. Server smtp.ionos.com, port 587, the user is the full address.
mail.helpGmail: Gmail: smtp.gmail.com, port 587. You need an “app password” (Google account → Security → 2-step verification → App passwords), not your normal password.
mail.internalHostHint: Optional. If the mail server is in your home network, enter its IP here (e.g. 192.168.178.116). The panel then connects to this IP but still checks the certificate against the name above.
mail.switched: Port {{old}} did not answer, port {{port}} with {{security}} did. That is saved now.

unreachable.title: Mail server not found
unreachable.tip: The name cannot be resolved or the machine does not answer. If the mail server is in your home network, enter its IP under “Internal server address (IP)”. An /etc/hosts entry does not help because the panel runs in its own container.

port_closed.title: Port closed
port_closed.tip: The mail server is reachable but accepts nothing on port {{port}}. Check which ports it listens on (Stalwart: usually 465 with TLS) and whether a firewall is in the way.

timeout.title: No answer (after 10 seconds)
timeout.tip: Nothing came back on port {{port}}. Often the name points to another machine from outside (e.g. NetBird) or a firewall drops the connection. Enter the mail server’s internal IP and try port 465 with TLS.

wrong_security.title: Encryption does not match the port
wrong_security.tip: Port 465 needs “TLS”, port 587 needs “STARTTLS”. Set the encryption to match the port.

tls.title: Certificate does not match
tls.tip: No secure connection: the certificate does not match the name, has expired or is self-signed. Enter exactly the name from the certificate under “Mail server” (e.g. mail.pmornhart.de) and put the IP only in the “internal” field. The check stays on for security.

login.title: Login refused
login.tip: User or password is wrong. With Stalwart the user is usually the full address, e.g. noreply@mornihosting.de. Enter the password again, save and test once more.

sender.title: Sender refused
sender.tip: The mail server does not allow this account to send as {{from}}. Use the account’s own address as sender or allow it for this account on the mail server.

recipient.title: Recipient refused
recipient.tip: The mail server does not accept this recipient. Check the spelling or try another address.

other.title: Unexpected error
other.tip: This matches no known cause. The reply below helps to look further.

quick.title: Quick start: done in a minute
quick.text: Just three things. The panel finds the mail server, port and encryption itself, saves everything and sends you a test mail.
quick.email: E-mail address the panel sends from
quick.emailHint: The mailbox you created for it, e.g. noreply@example.com.
quick.atHome: My mail server is at home
quick.atHomeHint: For example your own Stalwart in your home network. Then the panel also needs its IP.
quick.ipHint: The mail machine’s address in your home network, shown in your router’s device list.
quick.go: Set up and send test mail
quick.running: Looking for the mail server … (up to 30 seconds)
quick.allSettings: Set everything yourself (server, sender, sign-up, crash mails)

mail.registrationApprovalHint: After the e-mail is confirmed you are told (mail and Discord) and decide under “Approvals”. Until then nobody can log in.

mailPages.registerSent: We sent a mail to {{email}}. Click the link in it, then you can log in. Nothing there? Check your spam folder too.
mailPages.forgotText: Enter your e-mail address. We will send you a link to choose a new password.
mailPages.forgotSent: If an account exists for this address, a mail is on its way. The link is valid for one hour.
mailPages.resetText: Choose a new password for your account.
mailPages.resetDone: You can now log in with the new password. All other devices were logged out.

email_change.title: Address confirmed

register_pending.title: E-mail confirmed – almost there

mailPages.requestSent: An admin will look at your request. Once you are approved, you can log in with your username and password.

fields.spaceAgeHint: The Space Age expansion (with quality and elevated rails). Every player then needs it too.

games.noConsole: This game has no console for the panel. You manage the server in the game itself.

transfer.passwordHint: At least 8 characters. You need it on the new panel.

transfer.doneRestart: Done, all settings are taken over. The panel restarts now and reloads by itself.

stalwart.title: Connect Stalwart
stalwart.text: Running your own Stalwart mail server (free edition, 1.0 or later)? Enter its address and admin password. The panel then creates your mail domain and a sender account, sets up sending, sends a test mail and checks your DNS records.
stalwart.urlHint: The page where you log in to Stalwart, e.g. https://mail.example.com or http://192.168.178.116:8080 at home.
stalwart.passwordKept: Leave empty to keep the saved password.
stalwart.senderHint: The panel sends its mails from {{address}}. It creates the account itself, with a long random password.
stalwart.publicIp: Public IP of the mail server
stalwart.publicIpHint: Makes the mail server's name (e.g. mail.example.com) point to it. Leave empty if that record is already right.
stalwart.publishDns: Let Stalwart set its DNS records
stalwart.publishDnsHint: Stalwart gets the panel's {{provider}} access and adds MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC and more itself – and keeps DKIM keys up to date later.
stalwart.publishDnsNone: Only works when your domain is connected with INWX or Cloudflare under “Own domain”. Otherwise the card lists the records to add by hand.
stalwart.done: Stalwart is connected, the test mail is on its way.
stalwart.recordsManual: Add these records at your DNS provider

detail.off: Switched off – the records are listed below.
detail.no_provider: Your domain is not connected with INWX or Cloudflare in the panel. The records are listed below.

a.title: Mail server name (A)
a.tip: The mail server's name must point to its public IP. If your domain is connected under “Own domain”, the panel sets the record with the IP above – otherwise add it at your DNS provider.

ptr.title: Reverse record (PTR)
ptr.tip: Without it Gmail and others reject your mails. Only the owner of the IP can set it (your server host, look for “reverse DNS”) – not INWX.

mx.title: Domain inbox (MX)
mx.tip: Tells other mail servers where mail for your domain goes. Stalwart sets it once DNS access is handed over.

spf.title: Allowed senders (SPF)
spf.tip: Allows your mail server to send for the domain. Only one SPF record per domain.

dkim.title: Signature (DKIM)
dkim.tip: Stalwart signs every mail; the public key must be in DNS. New records take a few minutes.

dmarc.title: Forgery policy (DMARC)
dmarc.tip: Tells receivers what to do with forged mails. “v=DMARC1; p=none” is enough to start.

netbirdExit.title: Hide the home connection
netbirdExit.text: Everything the MorniHosting machine sends to the internet (downloads, mails, updates, the game servers themselves) then goes through NetBird and leaves at another NetBird machine – usually the NetBird server. Visitors come in through NetBird anyway. So your home connection's IP shows up nowhere.
netbirdExit.machineHint: The machine all internet traffic goes through, with its public IP.
netbirdExit.hidden: Your home connection is hidden. The panel reaches the internet through {{name}} ({{ip}}).
netbirdExit.notYet: The panel still reaches the internet through your home connection. NetBird needs a few seconds to switch – this card keeps checking. If it stays like this, the NetBird agent is not running on {{name}} or it may not forward traffic.
netbirdExit.leaksTitle: These addresses still point at your home connection:
netbirdExit.leaksTip: Delete their old A records at your DNS provider (e.g. INWX). The addresses should only point at your NetBird server.
netbirdExit.agentTitle: No exit to choose? Install the NetBird agent on the NetBird server
netbirdExit.agentText: Run once on the NetBird server (e.g. at IONOS). You get the setup key in the NetBird dashboard under “Setup Keys”.
netbirdExit.agentHint: Afterwards the server shows up here as exit (reload the page).
netbirdExit.dnsAutomation: The DNS automation under “Own domain” is on and would put your home IP at your DNS provider. Disconnect it there.

mailTests.title: Mail test
mailTests.text: Send a test mail to up to 5 addresses at once – e.g. Gmail, Outlook and GMX – and see live whether it arrived. With Stalwart connected the panel also shows what the recipient's server answered.
mailTests.addressesHint: Type an address and press “Add” (or comma/space). Up to {{max}} addresses.
mailTests.spamHint: Also sends to a mail-tester.com test address and shows the score from 0 to 10 and what costs points. About 3 tests a day are free there.
mailTests.untracked: without Stalwart: only followed up to your own mail server

spam.open: Result not available yet – open it on mail-tester.com

tips.retrying: The recipient's server has not taken the mail yet. Stalwart retries on its own. A certificate or connection error usually means the way out is blocked (port 25, forwarding).
tips.rejected: The recipient's server refused the mail. The reason is above – often PTR, SPF or DKIM is missing, or the IP is on a block list.
tips.failed: Your own mail server did not accept the mail. Check the login data above or “Connect Stalwart”.
tips.unreachable: The panel cannot reach your mail server at all right now (not a login problem). Is the mail server container running? On the Proxmox host: pct status <ID> – otherwise check the path in your home network.

team.title: Team
team.text: Give others access to this server – by username or e-mail. The role decides what they may do.
team.addText: The person needs a panel account. If they don't have one yet, they can request it on the start page with “Request account”.
team.whoHint: Upper and lower case don't matter.
team.roleHint: Moderator: start, stop, console, players. Viewer: look only. Owner: everything (only admins can give it).
team.removeText: They can no longer reach this server. Their account stays.
team.leaveText: You will no longer see this server. You only get back in if someone adds you again.

accessSheet.failed: The PDF could not be created. Please try again.
accessSheet.doneText: You only see the password now. Pass it on – nicest with the access sheet.
accessSheet.sheetText: A nice PDF with address, username, password, QR code and the first steps. Just download and send it.
accessSheet.intro: Here is everything you need to get started. You will be in within two minutes.

open.title: Open the panel
open.text: Open {{address}} in your browser – on a computer or phone. Or simply scan the QR code.

login.title: Sign in
login.text: Enter your username (or e-mail) and the password from above.

secure.title: Choose your own password
secure.text: On your first sign-in the panel asks you for your own password. Safer and easier still: then turn on a passkey or two-factor sign-in under “My account”.

admin.title: Set everything up
admin.text: You are an admin: the admin area holds domain, e-mail, updates and more. Create servers under “Create server”.

create.title: Order a server
create.text: Under “Create server” pick a game and a plan. One click later your server runs – address and console are on its page.

team.title: Your servers
team.text: As soon as someone adds you to a server's team, it shows up in your overview. You can request your own server under “Create server”.

accessSheet.javaText: On PC: start Minecraft › Multiplayer › Add server. Use the address from the panel (“Connect”).
accessSheet.bedrockText: Phone, console, Windows: Play › Servers › Add server. Address from the panel, port = Bedrock port (usually 19132).
accessSheet.warning: Please keep this sheet to yourself. The start password only lasts until your first sign-in.

forcePassword.title: Welcome, {{name}}! Choose your own password
forcePassword.text: An admin created your password. So that only you know it, set your own now – then you're good to go.
forcePassword.currentHint: The password you just signed in with.
forcePassword.nextHint: At least 10 characters. A sentence of several words is strong and easy to remember.
forcePassword.same: Please choose a different one than the start password.
forcePassword.done: Done! From now on you sign in with your own password.

playerDetail.listText: Everyone who has ever been on the server. Click a name for inventory, deaths, kills and chat – even while they are offline.
playerDetail.nobodyYet: Nobody has joined the server yet.
playerDetail.onlyOnline: Only works while the player is online.
playerDetail.noData: There is no player file yet. It is written as soon as the server saves the player (at the latest when they leave).
playerDetail.teleportText: The player is moved to these coordinates right away.
playerDetail.chatEmpty: The logs hold no message from this player yet.

payments.emptyText: As soon as someone redeems the voucher “MORNI” when ordering, you see here who owes you how much a month.
payments.note: The panel only remembers who owes what and which months you marked as paid. No money goes through the panel. Remember to declare income to the tax office.
payments.mineTitle: You pay {{price}} a month for your server.
payments.mineOpen: Still open: {{amount}}. Pay it directly to whoever runs this panel.

addOnSetup.running: Being set up automatically right now – you picked it when ordering. Usually takes less than a minute, then the server starts.

orderSetup.title: Setting up {{name}}
orderSetup.text: Almost there – the panel opens by itself as soon as everything is ready.
orderSetup.hint: You can close this page, the setup keeps going.

steps.pregen: Generate the world around the spawn

preload.title: Preload games
preload.text: Downloads a game before anyone orders a server for it. New servers then only copy it – seconds instead of minutes or hours (CS2: about 60 GB).

modes.template: Downloads the server program or game files once; new servers copy them.
modes.image: The game is already inside the program package – only the package is pulled.

preload.auto: Stays current by itself: the panel looks for updates every hour and installs them.
preload.autoChecked: Stays current by itself – last looked for updates at {{time}} (every hour).
preload.removeAllText: {{count}} preloaded games are deleted and free their disk space. Your servers stay as they are. New servers download the games again themselves.

publicStats.cardText: A page to share, no login needed: who is online, who plays the most, who died how often and of what.
publicStats.missingText: The server switched its statistics page off or the link is wrong.

impressum.title: Imprint
impressum.adminText: Upload a picture here (PNG, JPG or WebP, up to 10 MB). It appears on the "Imprint" page linked at the bottom of the start page – also without logging in. Make sure it shows your real details (name, address, contact).

via.title: All Minecraft versions
via.text: With ViaVersion and ViaBackwards (ViaFabric on Fabric) players on older and newer Minecraft versions can join. The panel keeps the plugins up to date automatically.
via.restart: Takes effect at the next restart.

playerCommands.title: Commands for {{name}}
playerCommands.locked: You're not on this server's whitelist yet. Ask an admin to let you in – then everything here works.
playerCommands.unknown: You haven't been on the server with this name yet – here's what awaits you.
playerCommands.allYours: You're an admin – you can use everything
playerCommands.missingText: This server doesn't exist or isn't a MorniCraft server.

mornicraft.title: MorniCraft
mornicraft.text: The panel's own plugin on this server: spawn, homes, teleports, messages, start elytra and sidebar. Set everything here – applies at once.
mornicraft.noPlugin: This panel lacks the plugin file (built without MorniCraft). The next update brings it.

fields.tabStats: Kills and deaths in the tab list

hints.back: Also back to where you died
hints.teleportDelay: How long to stand still (/spawn, /home, /tpa, /back). Admins go at once.
hints.maxHomes: How many places everyone may save with /sethome
hints.spawnProtection: Only admins build or break at the spawn
hints.sleepAtSpawn: Off: no bed and no respawn point at the spawn
hints.pvpAtSpawn: Off: nobody can hurt anyone at the spawn
hints.spawnRadius: The protection applies around the spawn point
hints.elytra: Jump off at the spawn and double jump = glide with real wings (survival mode only, no push upwards), no fall damage – your own chestplate comes back after landing
hints.elytraRadius: Gliding can only start within this distance
hints.creeperDamage: Off: creepers explode, the ground stays whole
hints.fireSpread: Off: fire stays where it was lit
hints.hardDragon: A stronger dragon with its own attacks – off: the normal dragon
hints.welcome: Big title and card – once per player
hints.sidebar: Time, game time, online, ping, commands – everyone can hide it with /leiste
hints.showLink: In /info and the welcome (needs a panel domain)
hints.tabStats: ⚔ kills and ☠ deaths next to every name
hints.graves: Whoever dies gets a grave with all their things and experience – anyone can open it and take the loot
hints.gravePrivateMinutes: For this long only the dead player (and the team) may open the grave, then anyone
hints.combatSeconds: Whoever hits a player or is hit stays in combat this long: no teleports, only chat commands, no start elytra – logging out then means death (things go into the grave). 0 = off.
hints.sit: Right click with an empty hand to sit, sneak to stand up
hints.spawnCommand: Off: nobody can teleport to the spawn by command
hints.homes: Off: no /sethome, /home, /homes and no clan base
hints.spawnLimit: How often everyone may use /spawn – e.g. once an hour or 3 times a day. Admins are exempt.
hints.spawnLimitHours: Time span of the limit (24 h = a day, 168 h = a week)
hints.homeLimit: How often everyone may teleport to a home or the clan base
hints.tpaLimit: How many /tpa and /tpahere requests everyone may send
hints.backLimit: How often everyone may go back with /back
hints.clans: Everyone can found a clan with /clan: menu, clan base, clan chat /cc, own tag (up to 4 characters) before the name in chat, tab list and above the head, no damage between members
hints.clanMaxMembers: How many players a clan may have at most (leader included)
hints.dragonDamage: 100 % = as strong as the normal dragon
hints.dragonAttackSeconds: How often it attacks with lightning, fire and the rest – twice as often in rage
hints.dragonRagePercent: With this little health left it rages: faster attacks, new end crystals
hints.dragonXp: On top of the normal experience
hints.dragonBrood: At ¾, ½ and ¼ of its health it calls phantoms for help
hints.dragonLightning: Lightning strikes where players stand – it sparks a moment before, whoever steps aside is fine
hints.dragonFireballs: Fireballs rain from the sky onto the players
hints.dragonFangs: Fangs shoot out of the ground round the players – smoke rises a moment before
hints.dragonEndermen: Endermen nearby go for the players, new ones come if needed
hints.dragonLevitation: Homing shots make players float up into the air
hints.dragonShockwave: Whoever stands too close to the dragon is thrown away
hints.dragonCrystals: When it rages, three end crystals stand on the pillars again and heal it
hints.dragonEgg: Normally the dragon egg only comes with the first victory

mornicraft.rulesHint: One rule per line – shown with /rules.
mornicraft.live: Saving applies at once, also while the server runs.
mornicraft.personal: Every player has a page with exactly their commands:

ranks.text: Symbol and colour in front of the name – in chat, in the tab list and above the head – and what the rank may do. The highest matching rank counts.
ranks.name: Name
ranks.everyoneElse: Everyone without another rank has this one.
ranks.autoHint: Automatically from the panel (linked Minecraft account)
ranks.isDefaultHint: Whoever has no other rank gets this one

permHints.reload: /mornicraft reload, give ranks in the game: /vip <player>, /mod <player> …
permHints.moderate: Jail, mute, freeze, team menu (sneak + right click)

ranks.badgesHint: A coloured tag with an own pixel icon and the rank's name. Players are offered a tiny resource pack when they join; whoever declines (and Bedrock) sees the symbols.
ranks.badgesNoDomain: Needs the panel's domain (admin area → Domain) so players can load the resource pack. Until then: symbols.
ranks.badgesRequiredHint: Java players load the badges automatically when joining – no "no" button. So everyone sees the badges. Bedrock shows symbols.
ranks.badgeText: Rank name next to the icon
ranks.badgeTextHint: Off: the badge shows only the icon (e.g. the crown). On: icon and name, e.g. “OWNER”.

teamBoard.title: Team dashboard
teamBoard.closed: This link is not valid (any more)
teamBoard.closedText: Type /teamdashboard in the game – you get a new link. The team dashboard is for moderators and owners.
teamBoard.noHistory: No punishments yet – a peaceful server!
teamBoard.rulesHint: One rule per line. Applies right away in the game (/rules) and in the settings.
teamBoard.saved: Saved – live in the game now.

doText.jail: The player goes to the floating cell and can only chat. Works even when they are offline.
doText.mute: The player can no longer chat. Works even when they are offline.
doText.ban: The player can't join the server any more – for a while or for good.
doText.kick: The player is thrown off the server and can come right back.

commands.title: Commands in the game
commands.text: What you can type in the game as {{rank}}.

settings.title: Server settings
settings.text: Applies in the game at once – the same switches as in the panel.
